channel.title: Pier & Point · Potrero Power Station Block 9
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Potrero Power Station Block 9 (Potrero Power Station), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Potrero Power Station Block 9: Block 9's record and map notes no longer say the D4D…
item.description: Block 9's record and map notes no longer say the D4D shows a 177 ft height: the '177' MAX', '110' MAX' and '102' MAX' labels in the Figure 6.2.3 inset are dimension lines, and its heights are 85, 65 and 35 ft plus Unit 3 at about 130 ft (with Unit 3) or 125 and 85 ft (without). The 2035 expected-completion milestone was removed: the May 2025 Chronicle line that the hotel's construction 'could be a decade away' is the reporter's narration about a start, not a developer estimate of completion. The summary no longer says the hotel incorporates a retained Unit 3 and now notes Unit 3 was partly demolished in 2023-24 (2024 annual compliance report); the map notes no longer call the site vacant land, and DataSF Parcels shows the footprint within active lot 4175028 (1241 Delaware St). The rooftop-bar, hotel-size and existing-structures facts were tied to what their sources say, and D4D publishers are shown as SF Planning. Source: SF Planning, Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final, 2020-02-26 (https://sfplanning.org/sites/default/files/documents/citywide/potreropower_D4D_final.pdf); San Francisco Chronicle, 2025-05-22 (https://www.sfchronicle.com/realestate/article/power-station-park-sf-20339020.php); California Barrel Company, 2024 Annual Compliance Report, 2025-03-28 (https://sfplanning.org/potrero-power-station); DataSF Parcels (https://data.sf.gov/d/acdm-wktn); SF Planning, Potrero Power Station project page (https://sfplanning.org/potrero-power-station).

item.title: Milestone · Potrero Power Station Block 9: Chronicle reports the hotel approved for… (May 22, 2025)
item.description: Chronicle reports the hotel approved for this site is slowed by the sluggish recovery of San Francisco's hospitality sector ('the hotel's construction could be a decade away', the reporter's words), and that the developer, Enrique Landa, proposes an interim waterfront park (Prequel Park) around the stack in the meantime (May 22, 2025). Source: San Francisco Chronicle (Laura Waxmann), 2025-05-22.

item.title: Planned · Potrero Power Station Block 9: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero… (Apr 21, 2020)
item.description: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement covering the adopted Design for Development, whose Land Use Table (Table 3.1.1) lists Block 9; the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date (Apr 21, 2020). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2025-11-14; SF Planning Department; SF Planning, 2020-02-26.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2025-11-14; SF Planning Department; SF Planning, 2020-02-26

item.title: Milestone · Potrero Power Station Block 9: Port memo (Item 13B) describes the… (Feb 20, 2020)
item.description: Port memo (Item 13B) describes the project's program; SF Planning's project page lists a 240,000 sq ft hotel (250 rooms) in that program (Feb 20, 2020). Source: Port of San Francisco, Port Commission, 2020-02-20; SF Planning Department.
